text:
maria: FYI I'm drafting an infra plan for the proxy-side shim to handle mixed v2/v3 API clients. Main goals: stable routing, minimal latency impact, and no behavior change for pinned customers. Thoughts?

thomas: +1. We need a deterministic routing key so we can route by client capability header and fall back to compatibility mode. Suggest `x-rw-client-version` and a per-tenant sticky route.

leo: watch streaming. multiplexing long-lived connections -> backend may need to demux KV caches per-model-version. If we attach tenant+version to the connection metadata, we avoid cache poisoning.

anya: also need telemetry hooks up-front. We should emit `compat_mode` and `detected_version` per request for rollout dashboards. Can we tag via envoy filters?

thomas: yep. Example Envoy HTTP filter snippet I prototyped: ```yaml
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
    inline_code: |
      function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
        local v = request_handle:headers():get("x-rw-client-version") or "unknown"
        request_handle:headers():add("x-rw-detected-version", v)
        request_handle:headers():add("x-rw-compat-mode", v == "v2" and "on" or "off")
      end
```
works for tagging without changing payload.

maria: Nice. Operational questions: 1) how do we ensure canary won't route v3 traffic to v2-only backends? 2) fallback policy when model variant missing?

leo: For 1) enforce capability gating in the routing table: route rules = {client_version, tenant_override, region}. Canary rule set should have strict match on `x-rw-detected-version`. For 2) fallback: define ordered fallback list in request header `x-rw-fallbacks: v3,v2` and let runtime choose the best available. If none, return 503 with structured error and telemetry event.

anya: Regarding rollout, propose phases: opt-in tenants -> internal infra tests -> 1% production -> 10% -> full. Each phase uses toggle in config service (no deploy). We should also enable `compat_mode=true` flag per-tenant for emergency rollback.

thomas: Agree. Also note connection draining: when we switch route target for live connections we must ensure existing streaming SSE/HTTP2 flows continue on old backend until close. Envoy supports connection draining with `max_requests`/`idle_timeout` but we'll need per-tenant grace window.

maria: Good catch. Add a short TTL on in-mem routing caches so new sessions see updated routes quickly but old streams remain for grace.

leo: One more: KV cache schema differences between v2/v3. We need a cache-key prefix with `ver:` to avoid collisions. Eg `ver:v2:<model>:<prefix-hash>`. That will double memory usage temporarily but safe.

anya: Telemetry fields we'll capture: `route_target`, `detected_version`, `compat_mode`, `fallback_used`, `cache_prefix`. Also delta on p50/p95 latency and token-cost per request.

maria: Ops checklist draft: - implement header detection filter (thomas) - add routing rules & config service toggle (infra-team) - add cache prefixing (runtime team) - telemetry events + dashboards (observability) - staged rollout plan (SRE + PM)

thomas: I'll drop the filter PR by EOD, include tests for header absence and malformed version header.

maria: Great. Next sync tomorrow 10am to confirm rollout windows. If anyone sees a significant perf regression in staging ping #eng-sre immediately. :thumbsup:
